facts: ProjLine projects the distance between two markers onto an existing line.
Angle2ln is the angle between two existing lines.

wits_jacobson_1975.citation: Jacobson A. The Wits appraisal of jaw disharmony. Am J Orthod. 1975;67(2):125-138.

downs_1948.citation: Downs WB. Variations in facial relationships; their significance in treatment and prognosis. Am J Orthod. 1948;34(10):812-840.

sources.claim: Peer-reviewed description of Jacobson Wits functional occlusal plane through first-molar mesiobuccal cusp overlap and first-premolar buccal cusps.
Functional and bisected occlusal planes produce materially different Wits appraisals; plane choice is not interchangeable.

wits_functional_plane_corrobation.conclusion: Facad OL using incisor midpoint OLa is a vendor bisected-plane variant and must not be claimed as strict Jacobson functional-plane parity.

downs_occlusal_cant_corrobation.claim: Peer-reviewed reconstruction of original Downs occlusal-plane-to-FH norm; occlusal plane bisects posterior molar occlusion and incisal overbite.
downs_occlusal_cant_corrobation.conclusion: Facad OL/FH belongs to the same bisected occlusal-cant family, but exact strict Downs parity remains unproven because OLp is only a manual vendor marker in inspected evidence.

tweed_triangle_corrobation.claim: Peer-reviewed description of Tweed diagnostic triangle as FMA, FMIA and IMPA formed by Frankfort, mandibular plane and lower-incisor axis.
tweed_triangle_corrobation.conclusion: Wits and OL/FH membership in Facad Tweed.cph is vendor-profile compatibility evidence, not historical Tweed-core authority.

OLa.definition: midpoint of upper and lower incisor tips

facad_definition.interpretation: projection of B-to-A displacement onto Facad OL
facad_definition.sign_semantics: Projection sign depends on ordered B-to-A vector and ordered OLp-to-OLa line; do not reorder.

dc_resolution.rationale: Jacobson Wits uses projections onto an occlusal plane; independent literature identifies the original functional occlusal plane using posterior premolar/molar occlusion, while Facad OL explicitly uses an incisor midpoint plus manual posterior point.

The Facad line family is compatible with a bisected occlusal-plane cant concept, but the exact posterior anchor is a manual vendor marker and is not proven identical to the Downs posterior bisector construction.

profile_membership_boundary.rule: Vendor profile membership is compatibility evidence, not historical authorship or canonical-analysis authority.

verification_note: Triggers exact-HEAD certification after adversarial fixes and provenance binding.
